recommendation: Keep the source fix as-is. It is a narrow correction to an active workflow page that aligns the remaining Option A limitation with the already-applied FHIR-11433 clarification without reopening broader workflow-pattern design questions.
issue_request: FHIR-11433 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core workflow clarification asking why workflow communication options focused on fulfillment rather than status changes; the approved resolution said to revamp wording to reflect that status changes are possible too.
initial_application: The 2016 workflow commit 839bf586d6c1cf9a322e122852f0cc49bcfed263 listed #11433 and added a communication-pattern convention that most patterns also apply to status changes and information requests, with local limitations identifying narrower cases. The 2017 workflow split commit 50f4d4fa6310c62b86614de57e4468358df07f6e moved this material into the current workflow-communications, workflow-ad-hoc, and workflow-management pages.
additional_context: The active source already contains the general FHIR-11433 clarification at source/workflow-communications.html:87-88 and Task-pattern benefits at source/workflow-management.html:61 and :121 that mention status changes or other updates. However, source/workflow-ad-hoc.html:58 still said Option A only worked for fulfillment requests and could not handle state changes or information, even though Option A covers create, update, or operation invocation. The page is in build scope via source/hierarchy.xml and publish.ini. No direct Zulip or Confluence evidence was found that reverses or narrows the Jira decision.
reconciliation: Changed source/workflow-ad-hoc.html so the Option A limitation now says fulfillment, status changes, information requests, or other actions fit the simple REST pattern only when expressible as the direct create, update, or operation invocation.
source_changes: source/workflow-ad-hoc.html: replaced the stale fulfillment-only Option A limitation with wording allowing fulfillment, status changes, information, or other actions when expressible as a direct create, update, or operation invocation.

related_jiras.note: Later Published workflow issue about cancellation support in ad-hoc workflow scenarios; checked as context for the neighboring cancellation limitation but not independently decided.
